name: What makes a backyard guest house an ADU in Los Angeles?

mainEntity.name: When does a backyard guest house count as an ADU instead of just a guest house in Los Angeles?
mainEntity.text: When does a backyard guest house count as an ADU instead of just a guest house in Los Angeles?

acceptedAnswer.text: In Los Angeles, the key difference is whether the structure functions as an independent dwelling. A backyard guest house with a kitchen, bathroom, sleeping area, and separate entrance is generally treated as an ADU. A structure without a kitchen is usually classified more like an accessory structure or guest house. This matters because ADUs follow a different permitting path, are easier to approve in many cases, and can often be used for long-term housing. Homeowners should confirm whether their intended use is purely occasional guest lodging, multigenerational living, or rental income, because that affects design, utilities, and approvals. The safest early step is to define the room program before design begins so the project is planned to fit the right category from day one.
acceptedAnswer.description: A backyard guest house usually becomes an ADU when it includes a kitchen or full independent living features. Without a kitchen, it is typically treated as a guest house or accessory structure. That distinction affects whether the unit can be permitted as a dwelling, rented legally, and counted toward property value.
